tables.title: COMPARISON OF MSE FOR THE SI, TAYLOR-SERIES AND PROPOSED METHODS; ARBITRARY ARRAY AND NEAR SOURCE
notes: A: SI method. B: Taylor series method. C: proposed method, [ (14b), (22b), (24) ]. D: proposed method, [ (14b), (14a), (22a), (24) ]. E: theoretical MSE of the new method = CRLB.

observations: Table 1 compares localization accuracy for SI, Taylor-series, and proposed methods on arbitrary array with different number of sensors (M=3 to M=10).
Row A corresponds to SI method, which has 'no sol.' for M=3.
Rows B–E correspond to Taylor-series method, proposed method using two different formula combinations, and theoretical CRLB, respectively.
All numerical values are exact transcriptions from the table; no rounding or interpretation applied.
The note below the table defines the method labels A–E and specifies the equations used in each case.
uncertainties: The text mentions 'theoretical MSE given by (26)' but equation (26) is not visible on this page; thus its exact form cannot be verified from this image alone.

The phrase 'near source' in the table title implies a specific simulation condition described in the text (e.g., source at (x⁰=8, y⁰=22)), but the table itself does not encode spatial coordinates — only MSE values.
Column headers use 'M = k' notation without explicit unit; context suggests M is number of sensors (dimensionless integer).
